tagline: Istanbul's central crossroads — loud, energetic, and the transport hub the whole city revolves around. Better for passing through than staying, but essential to understand.

items.name: Mandabatmaz
items.description: A tiny, legendary Turkish coffee institution hidden on a side alley off İstiklal. The thick, unfiltered coffee is made the old way. Worth the search.
items.tip: No sign outside — look for the alley just off İstiklal. One of the city's best kept (open) secrets.

items.name: Gezi Park Café
items.description: Simple café inside Gezi Park, one of the few green spaces around Taksim. A calm retreat from the square's chaos.

items.name: Tarihi Karadeniz Pide (Taksim)
items.description: No-frills Black Sea pide restaurant that's been serving the same excellent food for decades. Cash only, incredibly good value.
items.tip: Order the egg and butter pide. Don't expect atmosphere — it's about the food.

items.name: Cumhuriyet Meyhanesi
items.description: A classic meyhane near Taksim Square. Traditional mezes, rakı, live fasıl music on weekends. A proper Istanbul night out.

items.name: Çiçek Pasajı Restaurants
items.description: The 19th-century flower market arcade lined with traditional meyhane-style restaurants. Atmospheric and unpretentious.

items.name: Taksim Square
items.description: Istanbul's symbolic heart. The massive Republic Monument, Atatürk Cultural Centre, and the start of İstiklal Caddesi all converge here.

items.name: Gezi Park
items.description: The only significant green space in central Taksim. A welcome refuge with trees, paths, and views toward the Bosphorus.

items.name: Atatürk Cultural Centre (AKM)
items.description: The restored art centre on Taksim Square hosts major opera, ballet, and cultural events. Check the programme.

tips: Taksim is the city's main transport hub — metro (M2), buses, and taxis all converge here. Easy to reach, sometimes hard to leave.
The square itself is mostly concrete. The good stuff is on İstiklal and the streets running off it.
Mandabatmaz Turkish coffee is a 2-minute walk from the square and one of the best experiences in the area.
Avoid Taksim on national holidays and weekends if you dislike very large crowds.
